mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPI YoY > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where HOUST declines for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% MoM signals strengthening economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 45% of instances where INDPRO rises > 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a loosening monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS decreases.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than GDP (GDPC1) over a quarter, it signals strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth in QoQ
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 45% of instances where RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and falling nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2% signals increased borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 2% during a tightening cycle.
